newsitem.title: ITALY: Aeroporti Roma asks clearance for bourse take-off.
newsitem.headline: Aeroporti Roma asks clearance for bourse take-off.

text.p: Aeroporti di Roma, the state-controlled company which runs Rome airports, is rolling closer to privatisation and has asked permission to list on the Italian stock market, financial daily Il Sole said on Sunday.
The newspaper said Aeroporti had presented its request to stock market watchdog Consob on Friday and its flotation could take off as early as mid-July.

Il Sole said the total stake up for offer in the company, which runs Rome's Leonardo Da Vinci airport, was not yet known but state industrial holding Iri, which holds 73.58 percent, has said it will be between 25.62 and 49 percent.
The privatisation is to take the form of a public sale offer (OPV) on the bourse and a private placement with institutional investors, it said.

Shareholders will hold an extraordinary meeting on June 2 to discuss modifications to the company's statutes ahead of privatisation and they could set a ceiling of up to five percent on the size of stake a shareholder can have.

Il Sole noted however that timing of the sell-off was uncertain due to other privatisations in the offing, like the third tranche of energy giant Eni in June and the projected sale of Autostrade expected sometime in June or July.
If Aeroporti lost the July slot its bourse debut would be rescheduled after the summer.
The company boosted net profits 61 percent in 1996 to 90 billion lire and increased its turnover 11 percent to 1.16 trillion.
